title: Posing as the Dixieland band in Alexandria and waiting tables
summary: Papa Lane's group copies Dixieland Jazz Band records, is run out of town, and he works in a restaurant.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Oh, is there any more you can tell about that one picture we had here, Papa Lane's band?
Oh, do you remember, are they calling, as you say, some people call him Pansy Lane, the name he didn't like?
Well, we went as imposters. We got a job in Alexander, Louisiana.

We posed as the original Dixieland jazz band. And they had a beautiful Victrola on the Battle House Hotel on the porch. And these soldiers, you know, sit on the lawn and these people are guests. And they played the liver stable blues. And we learned it just note for note. Like, so one guy in the audience is a soldier. He says, look, I know the Dixieland band. Those guys are imposters. So the mayor made us get out of town.
So I was broke. I'm always broke on them jobs. So I didn't want to send home for money. It was only Alexander, Louisiana. Ain't far from New Orleans.

So I went to work in a restaurant. I didn't know anybody or anything. So I had to work 16 hours a day. So to work in a restaurant, I had a needle shot in my arm. The government kind of the soldiers. So this crazy noise breaks a needle off my arm. My arm swells up. So it finally got wet and I went in there. And that's where I learned how to haul a bowl of chili, a bowl of hell, and an oyster stew, a cemetery special. I learned all the waitresses things. I was getting $16 a week and all I could eat in 16 hours a day work. So I didn't stay there. I got enough fare to go back to New Orleans. Then there was a play there in this place where we had this picture taken. I got the Air Dome. Had this stock company. And I played a Jap valet. All I had to do was be made up like a Jap and walk in and say, dinner is served, dinner is served. That was my line. I got paid so much a night for that.
